1) Present Applications preferred under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are seeking for quashing of C.C.No.228/PW/2004 (old C.C.No.1/P of 2001) pending before learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, 28 th Court, at Esplanade, Mumbai arising Burjor Noshir Nicholson vs The State Of Maharashtra on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167162331/

sentences.text: The Applicants have arraigned as accused in the said case.

2) Heard Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Sanjog Parab for Applicant in Cri. Appln.
No.2269 of 2002, learned Advocate Mr. Thakur for Applicants in Cril. Appln. No.816 of 2014 and learned App Mr. Gavand for Respondent-State.
2.1) Record indicates that, Rule and interim stay in terms of prayer clause (b) was granted on 18 th July, 2002 in Criminal Application No.2269 of 2002.
The Respondents had waived the service.
3) That, M/s.Chakshu Enterprises (M/s.Chakshu) is a proprietary firm having office at B-14, Suraj Mansion, 1st Floor, Bhangwadi, Kalbadevi Road, Mumbai-2.
Informant Mrs.Chkshu Dilip Parikh is proprietor thereof.

3.1) On 24th September, 2019 an Income Tax Officer visited the premises of M/s.Chakshu and told the informant about certain Income Tax irregularities committed by a firm namely M/s.Rydham Tours and Travels (M/s.Rydham), having the same address of M/s.Chakshu i.e., at B-14, Suraj Mansion, 1st Floor, Bhangwadi, Kalbadevi Road, Mumbai-2.
Therefore, all the liabilities determined in the assessment proceedings would be saddled upon informant.

Thereafter,
on 25th and 26th September, 2019 informant's husband Mr.Dilip Parikh attended the Income Tax office for inquiry, as POA H. C. Shiv 02 APL816.2014.doc of the informant.

During the inquiry, the Income Tax Officer confronted certain Income Tax Returns and other documents of M/s.Rydham,
by which claims of large amounts of refund were made.
However, the handwritten contents in the said documents were in handwriting of Applicant-Vinod Kapadia.

Further, the Income Tax officer showed to Dilip Parikh certain challans and Forms No.16-A issued by M/s. Cambatta Aviation Ltd.
(M/s. Cambatta) in favour of M/s.Rydham.
These Forms No.16-A were also carrying the same address of M/s.Chakshu.

After perusing said documents, Dilip Parikh realised that, the said documents were signed by Aplicant Vinod Parikh, brother of Applicant Kiran Kapadia of M/s.Kapadia and Company, who were Chartered Accountant of the informant.
Thus, the said accused persons misused the address of M/s.Chakshu for the purpose of fraud i.e., to claim refund of large amounts from the Income Tax office.
3.2) Thereafter, Dilip Parikh met with Applicant-Mr.Rajnikant Shah, General Manager, (Finance) of M/s.Cambatta and explained him the situation.
Thereafter, Dilip Parikh met with Applicants Vinod Kapadia and Kiran Kapadia.

The discussion in the above meetings transpired that, from October 1996 to October 1999,
M/s.Cambatta Aviation Ltd. obtained false and forged bills from M/s.Rydham showing that, they had hired motor vehicles for their company for which large amounts were paid and on that basis they have claimed the expenses, deduction from the Income Tax and H. C. Shiv 02 APL816.2014.doc reduced their tax liability.
All the Applicants were involved in this fraud for which address of M/s.Chakshu was misused and it's employee Mr.Vilas Bomble was shown as proprietor of M/s.Rydham.
Hence, Dilip Parikh filed the private complaint bearing Case No.480/M/2000.
Considering the complaint, the learned Magistrate referred the same for investigation under Section 156 (3) of Cr.P.C.
In turn, police registered the complaint at M.E.C.R.No.4 of 2000 and conducted the investigation.

3.3) The investigation revealed that, between 1986 to 1999 the Applicants Vinod Kapadia and Kirit Pakai (accused Nos.1 and 2) in furtherance of their common intention opened fake companies namely M/s.Rydham Tours and Travels, M/s.Siddhivinayak Travels, M/s.Smita Burjor Noshir Nicholson vs The State Of Maharashtra on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167162331/
3 Travels etc. by misusing the address of the informant and witnesses.

sentences.text:
In the same transaction,
Applicant Mr.Rajnikant Shah (accused No.3) and Applicant Mr. Burjor Nicholson (accused No.5)
shared common intention with accused Nos.1 and 2, accepted the bills of said bogus companies,
approved the said bills, transferred the said bills amount in certain bogus bank accounts opened by accused Nos.1 and 2 and later on, all these accused shared those amounts and thus, cheated the informant and others and misappropriated the money of M/s.Cambatta.
Applicant-Kiran Kapadia (accused No.4) allowed his office to be used for that act by other accused.
Accordingly, the accused came to be charge sheeted showing the accused H. C. Shiv 02 APL816.2014.doc No.5 therein, as absconding.
4) Learned Senior Advocate Mr.Parab for Applicant Mr. Burjor Nicholson submitted that, there is no evidence that this Applicant was directly or indirectly involved in the alleged offence.
The Applicant has not caused any false representation or wrongful loss to the informant and witnesses.
In fact, there is no material to attract the offences of cheating, misappropriation etc. against the Applicant.
Thus, the Applicant is innocent.

5) Learned Advocate Mr. Thakur for the rest of the Applicants submitted that, even if the allegations made in the F.I.R are taken at its face value and accepted in entirety, it do not constitute the alleged offence.
There is no material in the charge sheet to show that the Applicants were involved in this offence in any manner.
It is submitted that, as alleged, these Applicants assisted each other to defraud the Government by claiming the Income Tax Refund.
However, the informant and witnesses cannot be said to be victim thereof.
After due enquiry, the Income tax department has exonerated the Applicant No.2.
The Income Tax levied upon the rest Applicants has been paid by them.
Therefore, no proceeding for penalty was initiated against the said Applicants.
As such, the prosecution of the Applicants in the said case would be abuse of process of law.
6) We have carefully considered the rival submissions and investigation material available on record.

It revealed that, informant H. C. Shiv 02 APL816.2014.doc Ms.Chakshu Parikh and the concerned witnesses, whose addresses were allegedly misused by the accused persons have not suffered any wrongful loss on account of the alleged crime.
The alleged forged/disputed documents submitted with the Income Tax department were not seized from the said department.

The investigation material does not show that, during investigation specimen of relevant signatures and handwriting were taken from the concerned witnesses and accused persons and the same were sent along with the seized forged/disputed documents to the handwriting expert for his opinion.

The prosecution has not disputed the contention that, Applicant Kiran Kapadia (accused No.4) has been exonerated by Income Tax department for the alleged fraud and that, the rest Applicants have paid the Income Tax levied upon them.
No statement of the concerned Income Tax Officer has been recorded to show that, the Income Tax department has initiated any other proceedings for evasion of the tax.
Similarly, the Income Tax department has not filed any F.I.R. or a criminal case to prosecute the Applicants for the alleged fraud.
7) In view thereof the prosecution of the Applicants in the said case would be abuse of process of law.
Hence, the said case is liable to be quashed.
Thus, we are inclined to allow the Applications.
